Hi Carlos — thanks for the note and the attachments. Short answers up front: we prefer two separate wires to each legal entity if possible (cleanest for VAT and local reporting). If you need to send a single wire in USD to Redwood Inc., we can accept and perform the inter-entity allocation, but we will need you to indicate both invoice numbers in the payment reference and select "Sender pays all charges" (SHA vs OUR vs BEN — OUR preferred for single-wire).

What to include in the reference: please add both invoice numbers separated by a semicolon: "INV4521;INV4522" and the Novus AP reference (e.g., NH-PO-8701). That ensures automatic matching.

I'm looping in Marissa (accounts) to confirm exact bank strings to use and whether Redwood will absorb intermediary fees for this payment. Karthik — FYI, this is a netting question for Novus; they may prefer a single USD wire for treasury convenience. Would prefer your take on commercial expectations.

Best,

Mina — thanks for the context. Quick notes from treasury:

- Preferred: two separate wires to the respective entities (Redwood Europe B.V. — EUR, Redwood Inc. — USD). This keeps VAT lines clean and avoids retrospective VAT reclaim work.
- If Novus sends a single USD wire to Redwood Inc., we will perform an internal transfer to Redwood Europe. We typically pass the correspondent/intermediary fees through as a separate line-item or a short reimbursement invoice unless the customer requests otherwise.
- For this account pair we can make a one-time concession to absorb up to $45 of intermediary fees (as a customer experience gesture) if Novus confirms the payment today and it's part of the renewal/expansion (deal D-4791-NH). Beyond that, fees will be billed back.

Bank formatting caveat: some banks trigger extra correspondent hops when the beneficiary name includes diacritics or long legal entity text. Please ask your bank to use the plain legal name exactly as below and include the IBAN / ACH routing without extra punctuation.

Redwood Europe B.V. (EUR receipt):
Beneficiary name: Redwood Europe BV
IBAN: NL77REDW0000001234
BIC/SWIFT: REDWNL2A
Purpose/Reference: INV4521;NH-PO-8701

Redwood Inc. (USD receipt):
Beneficiary name: Redwood Inc
Account: 123456789 (ACH/wire)
Routing (Fed ABA): 021000021
Purpose/Reference: INV4522;NH-PO-8701

I attached a concise bank account matrix and a PDF with formatting examples to avoid intermediary conversions. If Novus uses ISO20022 pain.001, include full IBAN/Remittance block.

Marissa
Head of Treasury Operations

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Payment questions — invoices 4521 / 4522 (EUR / USD)

Carlos — apologies for the longer note, wanted to be precise.

1) Intermediary fees and VAT: If Redwood receives a net amount (BEN instruction where intermediary fees are deducted), Redwood Europe will record the net amount received and issue a credit/debit note if necessary. That can complicate VAT reclaim in some jurisdictions. To avoid downstream VAT friction, our operational recommendation is: instruct the payer to select "Sender covers charges (OUR)" where possible for the EUR payment. If NH cannot do OUR, please ask the bank to send SHA but include a second short confirmation email to finance@redwood.com stating the gross amount sent so we can reconcile.

2) FX methodology for single-wire USD then internal allocation: we use the spot mid-market rate at the time of the internal intercompany sweep (timestamped when funds post to Redwood Inc.). We apply a transparent FX spread of 0.25% for internal recharges to cover hedging/operational costs. We will show the FX rate and calculation on the intercompany posting and provide a reconciliation file upon request.

3) Operational options (pick one):
  A) Two wires: EUR to Redwood Europe (OUR/SHA), USD to Redwood Inc (OUR/SHA) — simplest for VAT and bookkeeping.
  B) Single USD wire to Redwood Inc (OUR preferred). Redwood will allocate and invoice/credit the EUR portion internally. Novus must include both invoice numbers and NH-PO-8701 in the remittance. Redwood will apply spot rate + 0.25% FX recharge and either bill that as a separate small invoice or deduct from the amount attributed to Redwood Inc.

4) Concession: For this renewal we will absorb up to $45 in intermediary fees (one-time) if you can confirm payment by end of day tomorrow and select option A or B explicitly in your payment instruction.

Please confirm which option you prefer and we will issue final formatted wire strings for each entity. If you want, we can also schedule a 20-minute call with Treasury to walk through the SWIFT pain.001 fields and your bank's UI.

Best regards,
Marissa Cole
Head of Treasury Operations
